title: Audit a differentiable scientific inverse problem

stages.title: Simulation and numerical references
stages.evidence: Two rate/grid comparisons, shape diagram and an unstable-step diagnosis
stages.expected: PASS stage 1: two rates, grids, independent polynomial and exponential oracles, axes, invalid inputs
stages.diagnosis: If the polynomial matches but the exponential does not, test grid refinement before changing the implementation.

stages.title: Objective and solver sensitivity
stages.evidence: Independent scalar loss, two finite-difference probes and malformed-observation checks
stages.expected: PASS stage 2: independent objective, log-rate finite differences at two probes, malformed-target rejection
stages.diagnosis: If the derivative is zero but finite differences are nonzero, inspect detached arrays or missing dependence on log-rate.

stages.title: Parameter recovery and an inference report
stages.evidence: Changed physical rates, frozen held-out metrics, replay, refinement and noisy search comparison
stages.expected: PASS stage 3: changed-parameter recovery, frozen held-out metrics, replay, refinement, noisy independent grid-search agreement
stages.diagnosis: If fit is excellent but inferred rate changes with the grid, quantify numerical bias; do not tune against held-out observations.

rubric: Separate discrete algorithm correctness from continuous approximation error
Verify batch/time axes, singleton batches and malformed-input rejection
Check rate sensitivities against independent finite differences at two probes
Recover changed physical rates from independently generated observations
Preserve held-out data and prove deterministic replay
Compare noisy-data inference with an independent search
Report grid refinement, non-identifiability and limits of synthetic evidence
setupNote: Extract the project ZIP into a fresh folder, install its requirements-cpu.txt in your course environment, and run commands from the extracted top folder. CPU float64 is enabled by the scaffold.
